title: Round the pack, keep the remainder
hook: Seven guests, three snacks each, packs of ten: do you buy more than you need?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Round purchases to whole packs and compute excess quantity.

misconception: Buying whole packs provides exactly the required quantity.
objective: Round purchases to whole packs and compute excess quantity.

claims.text: Each guest receives three items. Packs contain ten items and cannot be split at purchase. Scaled model; quantity-only model; indivisible ten-packs.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Guests=7, A=30items and B=21items. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*",10,["ceil",["/",["*",3,"x"],10]]]; B=["*",3,"x"]; x denotes Guests. At x=7, A=30, B=21. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: First compute the exact requirement, then divide by pack size and round up. Purchased quantity is a multiple of ten. The gap is an explicit remainder rather than a change in portions.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Each guest gets three items; packs hold ten and cannot be split. For nine guests, how many items are bought? Correct: 30. Nine guests need 27; divide by ten and round up to three packs, so 30 are bought and 3 are left over.
